title: Silent Suicide or Fiery Alarm?: Regulated Cell Death—Apoptosis, Ferroptosis, Pyroptosis, Necroptosis, and PANoptosis on Trial — How biology shattered the 33-year 'programmed apoptosis vs. accidental necrosis' dogma: Ellis & Horvitz rescuing all 131 doomed C. elegans cells; Liu & Wang's holo-cytochrome c moonlighting switch; Degterev's Necrostatin-1 & RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL necroptosis; Shi & Shao's 18-nm Gasdermin D pyroptotic pores; Dixon & Stockwell's iron-GPX4 lipid-peroxidation ferroptosis; zVAD-fmk fate-flip kinetics, PANoptosome plasticity & why Annexin-V/TUNEL misdiagnose 80% of lytic deaths

teenKit.tldr: For decades, biology taught a simple lie: cells either commit quiet, orderly suicide or die messy, accidental deaths from trauma. Science just shattered that dogma, revealing a sprawling menu of fiery, iron-driven, and explosive ways cells choose to self-destruct.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how cells choose to die or blow themselves up is unlocking revolutionary treatments for everything from stroke damage and autoimmune diseases to aggressive cancers.
keyTakeaways: Your body eliminates 50 to 70 billion cells daily through programmed processes without you ever feeling a thing.

The old textbook binary of 'orderly apoptosis versus accidental necrosis' has been completely replaced by a diverse landscape of regulated cell death pathways including ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis.
Standard lab tests like TUNEL and Annexin-V misdiagnose over 80% of lytic, explosive cell deaths because they were invented back when scientists only knew about traditional apoptosis.

vocab.meaning: The classic, clean form of programmed cell death where a cell quietly disassembles itself into neat little packages swallowed up by cleanup cells without causing inflammation.
A regulated, violent form of cell death that mimics accidental necrosis by exploding and triggering inflammation, controlled specifically by proteins like RIPK1, RIPK3, and MLKL.
A unique type of cell death driven by iron-catalyzed lipid peroxidation, where cell membranes literally rust and fall apart from the inside out.
An inflammatory, explosive cell death triggered by infections where proteins called gasdermins punch massive 18-nanometer holes in the cell membrane, causing it to burst.

quiz.question: What was the core belief of cell biology for over thirty years following Kerr, Wyllie, and Currie's 1972 paper?
options: Cells only die when they run out of oxygen.
Cell death was a strict binary choice between programmed, quiet apoptosis and accidental, messy necrosis.
All cells live forever unless infected by a virus.
Cells never actively choose to die; they are only killed by external physical trauma.
quiz.explanation: Textbooks long taught a rigid binary dogma stating that cell death was exclusively either tidy apoptosis or chaotic accidental necrosis.

quiz.question: How does ferroptosis fundamentally differ from traditional apoptosis?
options: Ferroptosis is caused by an iron-dependent accumulation of lipid peroxides that destroys cell membranes.
Ferroptosis only happens in single-celled organisms, never in humans.
Ferroptosis is a completely random event caused by physical crushing.
Ferroptosis requires zero energy and happens instantly without any chemical reactions.
quiz.explanation: Ferroptosis is a distinct regulated death pathway driven specifically by iron-catalyzed damage to polyunsaturated fats in the cell's membrane.

quiz.question: Why do traditional lab assays like Annexin-V and TUNEL often fail when studying modern cell death pathways?
options: They only work inside living nematode worms.
They were built around the old binary dogma and misclassify over 80 percent of lytic, inflammatory cell deaths.
They are too expensive for modern laboratories to use accurately.
They can only detect cells that die from iron poisoning.
quiz.explanation: Because these older assays were designed exclusively to spot classic apoptosis markers, they completely misdiagnose the vast array of newly discovered lytic death mechanisms.
